lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Precious promises and growing in godliness
nodes.d: Peter says God has given all that pertains to life and godliness and great promises, and tells believers to add virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and charity to faith so they are fruitful and make their calling sure.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the qualities Peter says to add to faith?
ev: List the qualities to add to faith in 1:5-7
Say what Peter says God has given in 1:3-4
Explain what lacking these things means in 1:9

nodes.d: 2 Peter is a letter from Simon Peter urging growth in the knowledge of Christ, warning against false teachers and scoffers, and pointing to the certain day of the Lord and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 2 Peter warns about and what it tells believers to do?
ev: Name the three sections: growth, false teachers, the day of the Lord
Say what Peter wants believers to remember

nodes.t: Eyewitnesses and the sure word of prophecy
nodes.d: Peter says he will remind believers before his death, that the apostles were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty when the Father's voice spoke on the holy mount, and that prophecy of scripture came from men moved by the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the apostles did not follow cunningly devised fables?
ev: Say what the apostles saw and heard on the holy mount
Explain where Peter says prophecy of scripture came from

nodes.t: False teachers and the examples of judgment
nodes.d: Peter warns that false teachers will bring in destructive heresies out of covetousness, and shows that God judged sinning angels, the old world in Noah's day, and Sodom and Gomorrah while delivering Noah and Lot.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what examples Peter uses to show God judges the ungodly and rescues the godly?
ev: Describe what the false teachers do and why
List the three examples of judgment in 2:4-6
Say who God delivered in 2:5-9

nodes.t: The character and end of the false teachers
nodes.d: Peter describes the false teachers as presumptuous, greedy and following Balaam, promising freedom while enslaved to corruption, and says to return to the way of righteousness after knowing it is worse than never knowing it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Peter portrays the false teachers and why turning back is so serious?
ev: Name the charges in 2:13-15
Explain the saying about the dog and the sow in 2:22
Say who Peter compares them to in 2:15-16

nodes.t: Scoffers and the longsuffering of the Lord
nodes.d: Peter says scoffers will ask where the promised coming is, recalls that the world once perished by water and the present heavens and earth are kept for fire, and says the Lord delays because he is longsuffering, not willing that any perish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the Lord seems slow to keep his promise?
ev: Say what the scoffers claim in 3:4
Explain what Peter says they forget in 3:5-7
Say why the Lord has not yet come, according to 3:9

nodes.t: The day of the Lord and new heavens and earth
nodes.d: Peter says the day of the Lord will come like a thief with fire dissolving the heavens and the elements, so believers should live in holiness and look for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells, and grow in grace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Peter tells believers to live while they wait for the day of the Lord?
ev: Describe how the day of the Lord comes
Say what kind of people Peter says we ought to be in 3:11
Say what new thing believers look for in 3:13

nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.d: God sees the wickedness of man, finds favour with Noah, and saves him and his household in the ark through the flood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Noah and the ark?
ev: Retell why God sent the flood and how Noah and his family were saved
Say how Noah left the ark and what he did (8:20)

nodes.d: Two angels come to Lot in Sodom, the men of the city press against his house, and the angels strike them with blindness. They lead Lot, his wife and daughters out; the LORD rains brimstone and fire on the cities and Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Lot was brought out of Sodom and what happened to the cities?
ev: Describe how the angels protected Lot and urged him to leave (19:10-17)
Say what God did to the cities and why 19:29 says He remembered Abraham

nodes.d: Numbers follows Israel from Sinai through the wilderness: the census, camp and Levites, departure from Sinai, the rebellion at Kadesh and forty years of wandering, Balaam, a second census, and preparation on the plains of Moab for entering the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of where Israel starts and ends in Numbers?
ev: Describe the journey in Numbers in three stages: at Sinai, wandering, and on the plains of Moab.

nodes.d: Numbers 22:22-41 tells how the angel of the LORD stands in Balaam's way, the donkey turns aside three times, the LORD opens its mouth and then Balaam's eyes, and the angel tells him to go with the men but speak only what the LORD says; Balak then takes him up to the high places of Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Balaam's journey with the donkey and the angel?
ev: Say what the donkey saw that Balaam did not.
State what the angel told Balaam to speak (22:35).

nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 90: teach us to number our days
nodes.d: The speaker says the LORD has been our dwelling place in all generations and is God from everlasting, while man is like grass and a thousand years are as yesterday; he asks to be taught to number his days, to be satisfied with mercy, and for the work of their hands to be established.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 90:12 asks God to teach and why?
ev: Read 90:1-6 and 90:12-17 and contrast God’s time with man’s.

nodes.d: Proverbs begins with the proverbs of Solomon son of David (1:1), sets out a father’s teaching about wisdom and folly (1-9), gathers many short sayings (10-29), and ends with the words of Agur (30) and of king Lemuel (31).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the main sections of Proverbs and who is named as the source of each?
ev: Describe the main sections of Proverbs: 1-9, 10-22, 22-24, 25-29, 30, 31.

nodes.d: The proverbs liken honour for a fool to a stone bound in a sling, say a fool returns to his folly as a dog to its vomit, picture the slothful turning on his bed like a door on its hinges, and say strife ceases where there is no talebearer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list two pictures Proverbs 26 uses for a fool or a sluggard?
ev: Find three images used for the fool and the sluggard in chapter 26.

nodes.t: New heavens and a new earth
nodes.d: The LORD answers a rebellious people, saves a remnant of his servants, and creates new heavens and a new earth and Jerusalem a joy where weeping is no more and the wolf and lamb feed together.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the LORD says he will create in Isaiah 65:17-25?
ev: Say who the LORD preserves and who he judges (65:8-15)
Describe the new heavens and new earth (65:17-25)

nodes.t: Examples of judgment: unbelievers, angels and Sodom
nodes.d: Jude recalls that the Lord destroyed those who did not believe after saving a people out of Egypt, that angels who left their place are kept in chains until judgment, and that Sodom and Gomorrha suffer the vengeance of eternal fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the three examples of judgment Jude gives?
ev: List the three examples in verses 5-7
Say what Sodom and Gomorrha are set forth as
